scene_translation: The bartender polished a glass in silence, fixing his gaze on you. "Your grandmother used to come here often and tell me — that someday her grandchild would wander into this city." He reached behind the counter and set a small envelope quietly in front of you. "I've been holding onto it for three years now. I'm glad I can finally pass it along." On the front of the envelope, your name was written in faded ink; on the back, an unfamiliar crest had been stamped.
grammar_note: 【〜てはVする】The pattern 「来ては話をしてくれた」 expresses a repeated action — "she would come, and each time she would tell me." 〜ては links a recurring condition to what habitually followed it. It's subtly different from just 来て話した (a single sequence); the 〜ては implies the cycle kept repeating. You'll also notice the bartender's speech (〜てくれたよ、届けられた) is calm and measured — the register of someone older who chooses words with care.

The unfamiliar crest on the back is a new clue — likely the same symbol that will recur on objects or locations. The envelope's contents are still unknown. The woman in blue has not appeared; she may be connected to whoever stamped that crest. Inventory note: the old envelope is a key story item — its contents and the crest will drive Act 2.
